title: What If You Fell Into A Black Hole?
sources: NASA / ESA: event horizon, spaghettification (tidal stretching) near a stellar-mass black hole
Hawking radiation and the black hole information paradox (Hawking 1974; Page 1993)
LIGO/Virgo observations of black hole mergers; general relativity time dilation near the horizon

lines.text: What would happen if you fell into a black hole?
lines.caps: WHAT IF | YOU FELL INTO | A *BLACK HOLE?

lines.text: At first, you'd feel nothing at all.
But as you get closer, gravity starts to stretch you.
Your feet feel a much stronger pull than your head.
From far away, you'd look frozen at the edge.
That edge is the event horizon, the point of no return.
Inside, space and time actually swap roles.
You might see the entire future of the universe in a flash.
Then nothing. Not even light can escape.
But information can't just disappear, so where does it go?
Physicists are still arguing about that one.
So what would happen if you fell into a black hole?
